transcript.answer: The OpenTelemetry metrics API, unlike its tracing API, has no proxy meter. An instrument created from `metrics.getMeter()` before a `MeterProvider` is registered is therefore a permanent no-op. It never switches to the real provider after one is registered. In Lore, `libs/server-core/src/outbound/otel.ts` created its instruments at import time, and the entrypoint imported that file before `initOtel()` ran. As a result, `lore.http.requests`, `lore.tool.calls` and the other counters never recorded anything. The fix (PR #2652, ADR-050) moves the instruments to `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts`. That file looks each instrument up lazily on the global meter provider registered at record time, memoized per provider.

judgements.reason: The answer says there is no proxy meter, that instruments created before the provider is registered stay permanent no-ops, and that Lore now resolves its instruments lazily against the current provider, which covers everything essential in the gold answer.
